item.title: Build GitHub Skills: Custom Self-Paced Learning with the gh-skills-builder Plugi — Wed Oct 14, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto Great developer training shouldn't require a team of curriculum engineers.
In this hands-on Microsoft Reactor series, you'll learn to design, build, review, and publish your own **GitHub Skills-style exercises** — interactive, self-paced, issue-driven learning experiences that live right inside a GitHub repository — using the open-source **gh-skills-builder** GitHub Copilot plugin. Across the series we'll take a raw idea, workshop, or demo and turn it into a complete, validated learning journey.
You'll see how the plugin's **custom agents** and **Agent Skills** collaborate to handle each stage of the exercise lifecycle, so you can focus on *what* you want learners to master instead of the plumbing behind it.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: El día que la IA decidió trabajar en equipo (más JARVIS, menos Skynet) — Thu Oct 15, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto En los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la IA escribe código, genera imágenes o responde preguntas. Pero hay algo mucho más interesante ocurriendo: ¿qué pasa cuando varias IAs empiezan a trabajar juntas como un equipo real?
En esta sesión vamos a llevar esa idea a la práctica montando, desde cero, una factoría de software basada en agentes IA. Cada agente tendrá un rol claro —programador, QA, diseñador, incluso músico— y todos estarán coordinados por un agente orquestador (el “project manager” de toda la vida) que se encargará de repartir tareas, tomar decisiones y mantener el flujo de trabajo.
Lo interesante es que no será teoría: lo veremos en directo. Los agentes se comunicarán entre ellos, pasarán tareas y construirán algo real delante de nosotros. Sin guión y sin red, mostrando cómo funcionan de verdad estos sistemas cuando los pones a trabajar.

item.title: Who decides what matters – Us or the model? — Thu Oct 15, 11:30 AM
item.description:
This event will explore the paradigmatic commitments in the modelling of systemic transformation.
Clara Barbara Stephan Klinkenberg, a Master’s student at the University of Iceland, will present her thesis research investigating how various computational modelling paradigms differ in their capacity to represent systemic transformation, which she then applied to existing sustainability transformation models.
This presentation and Clara’s research are part of the International Ecological Footprint Learning Lab, a research partnership based at York University through the Ecological Footprint Initiative.

item.title: 👻 Ghost Tour of Queen West & Yonge Street 🌙 — Thu Oct 15, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 👻 Ghost Tour: Queen West & Yonge Street 🌙
### Restless Spirits, Strange Stories & Toronto After Dark
The thing about ghosts is… **they don’t always stay where they died.** Sometimes they linger in places they loved. Sometimes they remain where unfinished business keeps them tethered. And sometimes, apparently, they just really like a particular chair.
On this walking tour, we'll explore some of the stranger stories connected to **Queen West and Yonge Street** — from hospitals and theatres to music halls, historic buildings, and some rather unexpected places. Some of these people met their fate on these streets. **Most didn't.**
Ghosts are funny that way.
This is a **curated storytelling experience**, combining Toronto history, local legends, and some of the city's more unusual ghost stories. And don't worry — we're not going inside the buildings.

item.description:
Join us for an overview of practical strategies for using generative Al in teaching and learning to help students develop critical Al literacy skills and use Al tools appropriately. This session will offer guidance and strategies along with time for discussion and Q&A. All who teach at York are welcome!
